headline: Ghana Slashes Malaria Deaths by 98% Since 2011
meta_description: Ghana has reduced malaria deaths by 98% since 2011, with Cape Coast Teaching Hospital achieving two years without a malaria death.
summary_short: Ghana has cut malaria deaths by 98% since 2011, with just 52 deaths estimated in 2025. Cape Coast Teaching Hospital marks two years without a malaria fatality.
body:
Ghana has cut malaria deaths by 98% since 2011, bringing the disease from a major public health crisis to near elimination. Just 52 deaths from malaria are estimated across the entire country in 2025—a dramatic reversal from the toll the disease once exacted.

The scale of this achievement becomes clearer at the local level. Cape Coast Teaching Hospital has gone two full years without recording a death primarily caused by malaria, a milestone that reflects both improved treatment protocols and stronger disease prevention across the region.

The transformation underscores what sustained public health investment and strategic disease control can accomplish. Ghana's progress offers a model for other nations still battling malaria, proving that even diseases long considered endemic can be brought under control through commitment and coordination.

Only 52 malaria deaths estimated in Ghana for 2025
Cape Coast Teaching Hospital: two years without malaria death
